BiblicalUsage: Sha't is despising, contemning, and Ezekiel turns it on Jerusalem's neighbours: the daughters of Syria and the daughters of the Philistines despise thee round about. And the promise stands against them: there shall be no more a pricking brier unto the house of Israel, nor any grieving thorn of all that are round about them, that despised them.
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that the despisers become the thorns, and the thorns are taken away — God ends the contempt of the neighbours.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
